title: Invertibility of the affine K-injective reverse homology comparison
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, phi:B to A a ring homomorphism, f=Spec(phi), and i an integer. In the derived scheme-module categories [def-pc-derived-category], let I be an unbounded integer-indexed complex of structure-sheaf modules on Spec A [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], assume I is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and Q(I) has quasi-coherent cohomology. Put P=f_* [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], with its finite-limit preservation. Then the specified reverse comparison H^i(P I) to P(H^i(I)), defined as leftExactHomologyComparison(I.sc i,P) [def-pc-left-exact-homology-comparison], is an isomorphism. No descended transformation or uniqueness assertion is assumed.

source.place: 0AVW, proof, affine cohomology display; 06Z0, affine derived equivalence; 01I9(2), pushforward of associated module sheaves.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary natural isomorphism res_phi followed by tilde_B to tilde_A followed by P from the tilde/global-sections unit, pushforward/global-sections comparison and the tilde/global-sections counit. The latter counit is invertible on affine pushforwards of associated sheaves. Exact tilde and exact restriction of scalars imply that tilde_A followed by P preserves homology. The normalization identity for the explicit reverse homology comparison then makes that comparison invertible on every complex obtained by termwise tilde.

Use the affine derived equivalence to represent Q(I) by Q(J), where J is termwise tilde of a complex of A-modules. Bijectivity of Qh on maps into the K-injective target I lifts this isomorphism to a homotopy class J to I. Fullness of the homotopy quotient gives a chain map s. Naturality of the quotient/localization isomorphism identifies Q(s) with the chosen representative isomorphism; hence s is a quasi-isomorphism. Every term of J is quasi-coherent.
The affine resolution theorem applies to s:J to I and shows that termwise affine pushforward P(s) is a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply naturality of the explicit reverse homology comparison to s. Its square has invertible source comparison by step 1, invertible mapped homology map because s is a quasi-isomorphism, and invertible termwise pushforward homology map by step 3. Cancelling the latter proves invertibility of the specified reverse comparison at I.
